title: How to SUMIF with OR criteria (this value or that one)
task: Sum rows matching ANY of several values — East or West, two product codes, multiple statuses.

excel.note: The array constant makes SUMIF return one subtotal per value; SUM adds them.

google_sheets.note: Executed 2026-08-30: =SUM(SUMIF(A2:A6,{"East","West"},B2:B6)) returned 110 in Google Sheets against 160 in LibreOffice — 110 is the East subtotal alone, because Google Sheets does no implicit array evaluation inside a scalar function’s arguments, so only the first value of the array constant reaches SUMIF. SUMPRODUCT with added boolean tests gets the whole OR in one pass; =ARRAYFORMULA(SUM(SUMIF(A2:A6,{"East","West"},B2:B6))) is the documented wrap of the original. Both are documented Sheets syntax, carrying no executed result of their own.

explanation: SUMIF against the array constant {"East","West"} evaluates once per value — producing {110, 50} — and the outer SUM collapses them: 160. That is Excel and LibreOffice; Google Sheets returned 110 when we executed it, the East subtotal alone, so use the SUMPRODUCT form (or an ARRAYFORMULA wrap) there. This is safe for OR-of-EXACT-values because one row can't match two different values, so nothing double-counts (unlike adding overlapping condition SUMIFs). For OR across different COLUMNS' conditions, where overlap is possible, use the SUMPRODUCT pattern from the sumif-vs-sumproduct comparison instead.

extra_checks.label: SUMPRODUCT with added boolean tests does the whole OR in one pass
